input.prompt: Top-down view of a badly folded local newspaper lying on a dark wooden desk, drawn as a 1970s European underground comic panel: bold black brush-ink outlines, scratchy crosshatching, flat muted colors (dirty beige paper, mustard, olive, brick red), halftone dots in the shadows. The front page is rotated about 7 degrees counterclockwise and fills most of the frame; behind it the inner pages stick out crooked and creased, fanned out unevenly, with a dog-eared corner and a coffee ring. The front page has the masthead 'LA VOCE' in big old-fashioned black letters at the top, a thin double rule under it, then a large completely blank band of plain off-white paper for a headline, a blank rectangular frame for a photo in the lower left, and two blank columns of plain paper in the lower right. Apart from the masthead there is no text, no letters, no lines of text and no scribbles anywhere on the paper. 16:9, no border.

A newspaper photograph redrawn as a 1970s European underground comic panel in black and white with halftone dots: seen from behind and far away, a tall dark figure in a long waxed coat, wide-brimmed hat and plague doctor beak mask with two small glowing lenses walks up the muddy main street of a poor mountain village of today; villagers watch from half-closed doors and windows; old cars, power lines, a satellite dish on a crumbling wall. Grainy, high contrast. 4:3, no text, no border.

Edit the first image, a black and white halftone newspaper photograph drawn as a 1970s underground comic panel. Change only the plague doctor walking in the middle of the street, seen from behind: his mask becomes the one in the second image, a reference sheet of the mask and of the staff. Under his wide-brimmed hat, the dark leather beak of the mask sticks out to the side, held by leather straps around the back of his head; a boxy 1990s camcorder block is strapped to the side of the mask at eye level, with a coiled cable running down to a small battery box on the back of his neck, and its small REC light glows. In his right hand he holds the long black staff from the second image, with its T-shaped handle and a coiled cable along the shaft, its metal tip touching the mud. Keep everything else exactly as it is: the same drawing style, halftone dots, contrast and grain, the street, the houses, the villagers at the doors and windows, the cars, the power lines, the satellite dish, his long waxed coat and his hat. Black and white only. No text, no border.

This is a hand-drawn, comic-style illustration of a folded village newspaper lying on a dark wooden desk. In the masked area only, replace the newspaper's name LA VOCE with THE VOICE: the same heavy black slab-serif lettering, hand-inked and slightly worn, the same height and the same slight upward slant as the old name, centered on the masthead above the two printed rules. Keep the paper color, texture and everything else unchanged. The text must read exactly THE VOICE.
